                                     PROJECT NO. 59142

 REVIEW OF ERCOT’S                              §              BEFORE THE
 INTERCONNECTION PROCESSES                      §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 FOR LARGE LOADS                                §               OF TEXAS

                    ONCOR ELECTRIC DELIVERY COMPANY LLC’S
                        COMMENTS ON ERCOT’S PGRR 145

        Oncor Electric Delivery Company LLC (“Oncor”) appreciates the opportunity to provide

comments to the Electric Reliability Council of Texas’s (“ERCOT”) Planning Guide Revision

Request (“PGRR”) 145. Oncor is also submitting a version of these comments to ERCOT as part

of the PGRR 145 comment process. Oncor believes the proposed batch study methodology is a

reasonable step forward in the ERCOT planning process that will accommodate the multitude of

geographically overlapping large loads seeking interconnection in Texas. With that said, Oncor

believes that there are a few small changes the Commission and ERCOT should make to the batch

process, described below, that will improve its ability to help load interconnect in a systematic,

timely, and efficient manner.

1. The Commission should provide imminent guidance regarding the financial
   commitments required for a load to enter the batch study process and avoid
   incorporating language subject to change in the rulemaking.

        Oncor recommends that the Commission direct ERCOT to delete the language in Sections

9.7.1 and 9.7.2 of the proposed rule that defines the specific financial commitment and other

requirements that must be included in Interconnection and Intermediate agreements. These

requirements are in flux. They are currently being set by the Commission in Docket No. 58481

and have, even recently, undergone substantial changes. There is simply no need to attempt to

duplicate these requirements in the proposed ERCOT rule revision when they are being set

elsewhere by the Commission. Only the entrance requirements to the Batch Process are required

at this point.



                  ONCOR’S COMMENTS ON ERCOT’S PGRR 145 – PAGE 1 OF 5
 2. Oncor recommends that all projects that receive RPG approval by July 10, 2026, should
   be modeled as base load in the Batch Zero study.

       Oncor strongly recommends that large loads that were studied as part of prior ERCOT

Regional Planning Group (“RPG”) filings and have been approved by July 10, 2026 should be

modeled as base loads not subject to additional study under Section 9.2.1.1 of the proposed rule.

Given the timing of the ERCOT RTP process, many of these loads were submitted in 2024 or early

2025, were studied by ERCOT as part of the latest RTP, restudied by an interconnecting utility,

and then resubmitted to ERCOT in an RPG filing. These loads should be included as base load

because they have gone through multiple study iterations and are far along in the planning process.

It would only create uncertainty and distrust among interconnecting customers and waste ERCOT

and customer resources to negate years of prior studies and planning by forcing the full restudy of

these loads.

3. Oncor recommends that the new batch process should establish a minimum capacity
   allocation limit of 100 MW per entity.

       The current proposed PGRR 145 language describes a batch study process that would

allocate capacity to studied loads. However, it does not describe how the batch study process

would allocate capacity between qualifying loads in a given batch or how much total capacity each

batch would allocate. Oncor has learned, through its experience with interconnecting data centers

for the last several years, that there are minimum thresholds of capacity that these large loads

require in order to develop. For example, Oncor attempted to divide available capacity into smaller

quantities between many requesting entities. The feedback received from the loads indicated that

loads would financially commit to take their entire requested capacity, but smaller allocations

rendered projects financially infeasible without a commitment of additional capacity in the future.

Establishing a minimum allocated capacity limit of at least 100 MW per entity will help ensure




                  ONCOR’S COMMENTS ON ERCOT’S PGRR 145 – PAGE 2 OF 5
 capacity is allocated in a way that enables these projects to be financially viable and consume the

allocated capacity.

4. ERCOT or the certificated retail utilities should backfill allocated capacity when a load
   elects to not move forward.

       The refinement process envisioned in PGRR 145 can be avoided by allowing ERCOT or

the certificated retail utilities to fill outstanding capacity requests with abandoned capacity. Oncor

recommends that ERCOT or the Commission modify Section 9.7.3 to expressly state that ERCOT

or the certificated retail utility reallocate available capacity to other customers in the same

geographic area seeking interconnection within the same batch.

       The goal of the batch process is to allow interconnecting loads to efficiently claim and

utilize available capacity on the ERCOT system. Once ERCOT has made a determination that

capacity exists in a geographic area and the studied load does not wish to accept that capacity,

other loads in the same geographic area should be able to step forward without waiting for the next

batch study that may be a year or more away. As new loads commit to take more and more

abandoned capacity, the need for the study refinement envisioned in the PGRR becomes

unnecessary. This will reduce ERCOT workload, enhance timely allocation of capacity, and

eliminate the uncertainty involved with additional iterations of ERCOT study.

5. The Commission should address the misalignment between Year 6 allocated capacity
   and the lack of identified transmission facility needs in PGRR 145.

       Proposed Planning Guide Section 9.3.2(3) sets the total load to be served in Year 6 (2033)

to the sum of interconnecting large loads’ requested amounts without creating a transmission

planning process that would actually determine the transmission facilities required to provide the

promised capacity in Year 6. The result is that the Batch Zero study will only plan transmission

projects that can be implemented within the batch study horizon and leave future, needed




                   ONCOR’S COMMENTS ON ERCOT’S PGRR 145 – PAGE 3 OF 5
 transmission projects for the RPG or Regional Transmission Plan process with no guarantee that

they will be constructed in time for the load. Oncor suggests that the Commission and ERCOT

work to find a solution for proactively planning all transmission projects needed for the capacity

promised by the batch study process. Oncor notes that several commenters have proposed viable,

potential solutions to this disconnect in the current PGRR.

                                     I.   CONCLUSION

       Oncor appreciates the opportunity to assist with ERCOT’s and the Commission’s

evaluations pursuant to PGRR 145.




                  ONCOR’S COMMENTS ON ERCOT’S PGRR 145 – PAGE 4 OF 5
